references.text: The land could not support them living together, for their possessions were so great that they could not dwell together.
Lot chose the whole Jordan Valley for himself and journeyed eastward. Thus they separated from each other. Abram settled in the land of Canaan, while Lot lived among the cities of the valley.

Esau took his wives, sons, daughters, all who belonged to his household, his livestock, all his cattle, and all the property he had acquired in the land of Canaan, and went to another land away from his brother Jacob.
